 ATP Finals Alexander Zverev beats Arthur Fils in ATP Finals tennis group stage – as it happened
 The world No 1 made it three straight-sets wins out of three to finish top of his group ahead of Ben Shelton, who also qualifies for the semi-finals
  Updated  9m ago Katy Murrells Thu 19 Nov 2026 16.48 EST First published on Thu 19 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 31m ago Zverev beats Fils 6-4, 7-6 (6) 
 2h ago Zverev wins the first set 6-4 
 3h ago Preamble 
 Alexander Zverev celebrates after defeating France's Arthur Fils. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP View image in fullscreen Alexander Zverev celebrates after defeating France's Arthur Fils. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP Katy Murrells Thu 19 Nov 2026 16.48 EST First published on Thu 19 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 31m ago Zverev beats Fils 6-4, 7-6 (6) 
 2h ago Zverev wins the first set 6-4 
 3h ago Preamble 
 20m ago 16.37 EST Jamie Murray thinks tonight was the “most entertaining match we’ve seen this week … to see Arthur in full flow is very exciting” . Fils’ stats weren’t far behind Zverev’s for the match, but he had a few moments when his attention wavered, and the world No 1 made him pay for that. Zverev wasn’t entirely convincing from the baseline, but his serve saw him through, and in the semi-finals he’ll play Daniil Medvedev or Frances Tiafoe, who meet tomorrow night in a winner-takes-all encounter.
 Carlos Alcaraz is guaranteed to finish top of the Ivan Lendl group, regardless of his result against Flavio Cobolli in the afternoon, though it’ll be interesting to see what physical state Alcaraz is in, having had an MRI today on his hamstring. Alcaraz is expected to play despite the injury, and I’ll be back with coverage of that match. Until then, ciao !
 Share Updated at  16.48 EST 27m ago 16.30 EST Zverev is asked on court about the injury: 
 double quotation mark Unfortunately I started feeling my ankle again. I’ll probably feel it for the rest of my career, it’s something I have to live with [he tore multiple ligaments in his ankle back in 2022]. But I hope I’ll be 100% fit on Saturday [for the semi-final] and I’m very happy to win all three matches against difficult opponents, Arthur especially, with all the power he has.
 Share 31m ago 16.26 EST Zverev beats Fils 6-4, 7-6 (6)
 A collective gasp as Fils surrenders in a backhand face-off, sliding a meek slice into the net … and it gives Zverev a sixth MP at 7-6 . It’s on the world No 1’s serve … another absorbing exchange plays out … and this time Zverev emerges victorious when he eventually knifes away a backhand volley! What a brilliant breaker to end the match; Fils definitely saved his best until last. But Zverev wins in straight sets to secure top spot in the John McEnroe group, Shelton goes through at his good friend Fils’ expense and Zverev remains on course to end his transformative season with a third ATP Finals title. Even though tonight’s performance was slightly patchier than his first two matches, Zverev still hasn’t been broken or dropped a set.
 Share Updated at  16.42 EST 36m ago 16.20 EST Another flash of Fils’ forehand and it’s 6-5, four match points saved, and they’re back on serve! Now Fils is cracking his backhand for a winner for equilibrium’s sake … and, improbably, it’s five match points saved and they change ends at 6-6 …! 
 Share 38m ago 16.18 EST Fils is rolling his eyes as he walks to the other side of the court, gone is the raw energy and belief he had at the start of this tie-break, and Fils doesn’t even move to Zverev’s ace, which brings up 6-1 and five match points. Zverev will be relieved to get this over with quickly, if he is struggling with injury, but some French resistance makes it 6-3 … and then 6-4 with a flicked forehand cross-court winner after quite possibly the longest point of the match! 
 Share 42m ago 16.14 EST HUGE hitting on the first point – hopefully the rest of the breaker continues in similar style – and Fils blasts his way to 1-0 before Zverev comes back for 1-1. Zverev seems troubled by his ankle or foot, and takes extra time before serving … he wins the point but still seems bothered, not that you’d know it when he biffs a backhand winner down the line for 3-1 before being gifted a second mini-break by Fils for 4-1 … and it’s 5-1 Zverev at the change of ends … 
 Share Updated at  16.27 EST 47m ago 16.10 EST Second set: Zverev 6-4, 6-6 Fils* (*denotes next server) 
 … Fils then rips up the script, getting to 15-all when Zverev makes an absolute mess of a drive volley, then 30-all with a blazing backhand winner and 30-40, set point, when Zverev errs with his backhand! But Fils is wincing when he misses a makeable return. He should have done better. Though he gets a second set point when Zverev blinks with a forehand! Zverev’s missed more of those today than he did in his first two matches combined. But Zverev then ups his game, taking three points on the spin, and tie-break time it is.
 Share Updated at  16.40 EST 1h ago 15.59 EST Second set: Zverev* 6-4, 5-6 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 … which moves a game closer when Fils holds to 15, the highlight the fourth point after some quality hitting on both sides of the net ..
 Share 1h ago 15.58 EST Second set: Zverev 6-4, 5-5 Fils* (*denotes next server) 
 Perhaps Ivanisevic was trying to give him some tips on how to neutralise Zverev’s serve. It doesn’t work, though, as Zverev holds to love. We’re very much on course for a tie-break …
 Share 1h ago 15.57 EST Second set: Zverev* 6-4, 4-5 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 Now we’re reaching the business end of the set, will Fils start to feel any pressure? No – as he advances to 40-15, courtesy of an unforced forehand error from Zverev (there have been several of those tonight) – and Fils is sprinting back to his chair after nudging 5-4 ahead. He’s playing with the freedom of a man with absolutely nothing to lose, knowing that he can’t qualify for the semi-finals, having lost the first set. And his coach, Goran Ivanisevic, is shouting some encouragement to him at the changeover – not that I caught a word of it.
 Share 1h ago 15.52 EST Second set: Zverev 6-4, 4-4 Fils* (*denotes next server) 
 There’s not much giving on serve again, as Fils flies through for 4-3, before Zverev is zooming along at 15-0, 30-0, 40-0. An errant forehand makes it 40-15, but it’s only a brief interruption from normal service, as another unreturned serve brings Zverev back level in this second set.
 Share 1h ago 15.48 EST Second set: Zverev 6-4, 3-3 Fils* (*denotes next server) 
 The fifth game is much shorter than the fourth, as Fils holds with little jeopardy, showing far more flair in his play than I did earlier with my Italian , as Simon Wylie emails to tell me it’s “ Rimanete sintonizzati !” not “ Rimani sintonizzato !” when addressing an audience. Noted, Simon. Grazie ! But I digress. Zverev cancels out Fils’ hold with an effortless one of his own.
 Share 1h ago 15.39 EST Second set: Zverev 6-4, 2-2 Fils* (*denotes next server) 
 Ooohs and aaaahs on the second point, which Zverev wins at the net for 15-all. He just misses the sideline on the third point and Fils has a sniff at 15-30. So Zverev, of course, rams a serve down the T and wins the point on his next shot … but Fils takes Zverev to deuce for the first time when Zverev’s backhand hits the tape and doesn’t go over the net! Fils fails with an attempted lob at deuce … but then lands one bang on the baseline at Zverev’s advantage! The crowd are celebrating as if Fils has won the match. But that’s as good as it gets for the young Frenchman, with an unreturned serve and ace sealing his fate.
 Share 1h ago 15.32 EST Second set: Zverev* 6-4, 1-2 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 Perhaps the biggest cheer of the night as Fils lets off the fireworks on his forehand, with an explosive passing winner down the line. He’s celebrating as if he still believes he can win this match, even though he can’t now qualify having lost the first set. It gives Fils 30-15 … and another fizzing forehand makes it 40-15, before he claims the game with his fourth ace of the evening.
 Share Updated at  15.39 EST 1h ago 15.28 EST Second set: Zverev 6-4, 1-1 Fils* (*denotes next server) 
 Zverev’s serving stats for the first set are on a level with his opening two matches. Six aces, zero double faults, zero break points, 76% of first serves in and 89% of first-serve points won. Fils, undeterred, opens the second set with a hold of his own, but Zverev is soon back doing what Zverev does, holding with ease, and he nearly takes Fils’ head off with a snarling serve as he wraps up the game to 15. “Zverev has taken power serving and consistency to a different level,” says an approving Tim Henman on the Sky commentary.
 Share 2h ago 15.22 EST Zverev wins the first set 6-4
 Zverev, serving for the opening set, fires down a message from the off with an ace. Fils somehow manages to get a racket on Zverev’s next serve, but Fils is pulled so far out wide and Zverev batters into the open court for 30-0. An unreturned serve makes it 40-0, and with four swats of the racket Zverev has three set points. And he needs only one of those. Fils’ tournament is over. Well not immediately, he’s got at least another set to contest, but he can’t qualify. Shelton will. And Zverev wins the group.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP Share Updated at  15.47 EST 2h ago 15.17 EST First set: Zverev* 5-4 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 Zverev holds comfortably to 15, with Fils still unable to take charge of the longer rallies, and it leaves Fils serving to stay in the set – and tournament – at 5-3. A brilliant backhand from Zverev – it’s one of the best shots in the men’s game, no doubt about that – and the world No 1 is applying the pressure at 15-all. And then 30-all. A gutsy one-two punch from Fils prevents Zverev from getting himself a set point, and Fils is fist-pumping when he secures the game. He’s down but not quite out just yet.
 Share 2h ago 15.12 EST Zverev breaks: Zverev* 4-3 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 Fils undoes ALL of his hard work on serve, with three unforced errors, including a messy skewed drop shot and a double fault. It leaves Zverev with three break points at 0-40. Zverev turns into pre-grand slam winner Zverev on the first two, going all cautious, but he holds firm on the third and Fils flashes long. The first break is Zverev’s – so Fils will now have to do something that no player has managed this week and break Zverev if he’s to advance to the semi-finals. Fils has to win in straight sets to go through.
 Share 2h ago 15.07 EST First set: Zverev* 3-3 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 An inauspicious start from Zverev, as he balloons long, but that’s the only blot in his service book in this game, as he reels off the next four points, finishing off with a backhand volley, which he stretches every sinew of his 6ft 6in frame to reach. Another very tall man, Nick Woltemade, currently on loan at Juventus, applauds approvingly in the crowd.
 Share 2h ago 15.03 EST First set: Zverev* 2-3 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 Fils unwinds with a vicious inside-in forehand for 30-0 – he’s still lost only one point on serve, that’s a Zverev-like stat – and it’s soon 40-0. And game. If he can continue to take care of business on his own serve like this, perhaps he’ll give himself the chance of a tie-break against the world No 1, with Fils knowing he must win in straight sets to qualify for the semi-finals.
 Share 2h ago 14.58 EST First set: Zverev 2-2 Fils* (*denotes next server) 
 Not immediately, as Zverev zips to 30-0, but Fils’ forehand is ON on the next point and he finds the sideline with a return winner. 30-15. Fils then blinks on his backhand for 40-15 in a more prolonged exchange; the Frenchman knows he’ll need to keep the points shorter tonight if he’s to prevail. And Zverev sees out the game to 15.
 Share 2h ago 14.55 EST First set: Zverev* 1-2 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 Fils, determined not to be outdone on serve though, secures the first love hold of the match. He always plays with so much energy and élan and is skipping back to his chair after that quicker than quick hold. He looks up for this … but can he make further inroads on Zverev’s serve?
 View image in fullscreen Arthur Fils whips a backhand to Zverev. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters Share Updated at  14.57 EST 2h ago 14.52 EST First set: Zverev 1-1 Fils* (*denotes next server) 
 Zverev’s serving stats this week have been quite ridiculous. Against Shelton on Tuesday he won 25 consecutive points on his serve, but he concedes the opening point here and then slides 15-30 down. Cue – of course – an ace to get him out of trouble. And he doesn’t give Fils another look-in from there. That’s 25 aces for the tournament now.
 Share 2h ago 14.48 EST First set: Zverev* 0-1 Fils (*denotes next server) 
 Fils starts as he means to go on with a short opening point. And the second is just as punchy too. A longer rally plays out on the third, before Zverev eventually flings a forehand long. So it’s 40-0. Fils concedes his first point with a mis-hit forehand – his forehand is the fastest and heaviest on tour, but that one won’t make the match highlights reel – though the cross-court forehand winner that seals the game will do. Fils opens with a hold to 15.
 View image in fullscreen Zverev in early action against Fils. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP Share Updated at  14.50 EST 2h ago 14.43 EST Remember: anything other than a straight-sets win for Fils will mean Zverev tops the group and Shelton advances alongside him.
 Share 2h ago 14.42 EST As for their head-to-head, it’s no surprise that the French and US Open champion, who is also a two-time ATP Finals champ, leads the ATP Finals debutant 5-2. Zverev has also won their two most recent matches, including this year in the Indian Wells quarter-finals, and their only previous meeting indoors, at the Paris Masters two years ago.
 Share 2h ago 14.38 EST The lights go out in the stadium. The sound of a bouncing ball over the speakers is mimicking that of a heartbeat. Fils arrives first, chewing gum, and looking very calm … and now here’s Zverev, dressed also in black but channelling his inner Federer with a gold bag. He’s ditched the jacket he wore the other day with 1 on the back. Perhaps he feels as if he doesn’t need to remind people of his new status given the supremacy of his two performances so far this week.
 Share 2h ago 14.30 EST Jamie Murray is talking on Sky Sports and says Zverev was “smoking the ball” in practice earlier. Which is ominous for Fils . He’s then asked which players are most likely to close the gap on Zverev/Sinner/Alcaraz next year. He thinks Fils has got as good a chance as any, given he doesn’t have many points to defend at the grand slams in 2027, having missed this year’s Australian Open and French Open through injury and lost in the US Open first round. It shows how brilliant the 22-year-old’s been away from the slams that he’s still managed to climb to a career-high ranking of No 7. Along with Rafael Jodar, Jakub Mensik and Joao Fonseca, he may well represent the future of tennis.
 Share Updated at  14.30 EST 3h ago 14.12 EST Two players who are definitely going home, though, are Britain’s Henry Patten and Finland’s Harri Heliovaara . The top seeds and defending champions in the doubles, who won the Wimbledon title for the second time in the summer, have lost their winner-takes-all match against the French pair Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti, 7-6 (5), 7-6 (3), with Patten appearing to be struggling with illness.
 View image in fullscreen Henry Patten (right) and Harri Heliovaara are out of the doubles. Photograph: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images Share 3h ago 14.02 EST There were concerns earlier that Carlos Alcaraz could pull out of the tournament after he cancelled his practice session and went for an MRI on his injured left hamstring instead. But the reports from Spain are that he’ll be OK to continue. Alcaraz – who qualified for the semi-finals with a match to spare – is scheduled to play the already eliminated Flavio Cobolli in the afternoon session tomorrow.
 View image in fullscreen Carlos Alcaraz suffered the hamstring injury in his win over Daniil Medvedev yesterday. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP Share 3h ago 13.50 EST Share 3h ago 13.47 EST Here’s the Associated Press’s report on Shelton’s victory: 
 US Open finalist Ben Shelton did his part. Now he needs some help from top-ranked Alexander Zverev to advance at the ATP Finals. 
 Shelton twice aced his way out of trouble in the first-set tie-break and beat Rafael Jodar 7-6 (8), 7-5 on Thursday. 
 If Zverev wins a set against Arthur Fils later in the final match of the group, Shelton will reach the semi-finals of the elite event for the season’s top eight players. 
 Zverev has already advanced with two wins, while Fils is 1-1. Fils’ only chance of advancing is by beating Zverev in straight sets. 
 Shelton beat Fils in his opening match and is good friends with the Frenchman. 
 “I’m always rooting for him,” Shelton said of Fils. “If he takes Sascha out in straights, I’m going to say ‘too good’ and go on holidays. I would love to make the semi-finals here for the first time. I did my job today and let’s see what happens. I’ll definitely be watching.” 
 The 20-year-old Spaniard Jodar, who was eliminated after losing all three of his matches, was the first man to qualify for the ATP Finals in the same season as his tour-level debut. 
 “Rafa is one of the best young talents that tennis has seen in a long time,” Shelton told the crowd. “To be here playing in Turin in his first year on tour, starting the year outside of top 100, is a ridiculous feat. So I hope all you guys recognise how special that is.” 
 Carlos Alcaraz has already advanced from the other group. 
 No matter if Shelton reaches the semi-finals or not, winning two of his three group matches is quite an improvement compared with when he lost all three during his debut at ATP Finals last year. 
 Late in the first set, a shot from Shelton clipped the net and hit Jodar in the back at the net. Jodar ended up on the ground and grasped his back when he got up but did not appear bothered as the match wore on. Shelton asked Jodar if he was OK and the players slapped hands. 
 In the final game of the match, Shelton slipped and fell over backward. But he got right back up and served three straight aces to finish it off. 
 In all, Shelton had 14 aces to Jodar’s nine, with the American’s fastest serve clocking in at 146 mph. 
 View image in fullscreen Ben Shelton lost all of his group matches on his ATP Finals debut last year but has won two out of three this time. Photograph: Stefano Guidi/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.53 EST 3h ago 13.30 EST Preamble
 Buonasera ! And welcome to our coverage of the last match in the John McEnroe group: Alexander Zverev v Arthur Fils.
 After Ben Shelton’s 7-6 (8), 7-5 win over Rafael Jodar earlier, Fils doesn’t need to pack a calculator in his racket bag because the maths is simple: only a straight-sets win tonight will put him into the semi-finals at Shelton’s expense.
 Zverev has the comfort of knowing he’s already through, with two wins from two at a tournament he’s won twice before, though he does have a cloud hanging over his name after yesterday’s news that he’s facing a new lawsuit , filed by his former partner, who alleges he misrepresented the outcome of his domestic abuse trial. The murmurs around his status as the new world No 1 – achieved in a year when Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have missed many months through injury – may have quietened a little after his two commanding performances in Turin so far, but he remains a polarising figure at the top of the game.
 The explosive talent Fils, meanwhile, is generating plenty of excitement on tour, having risen to a career-high world No 7 under Goran Ivanisevic’s guidance despite having played only three grand slam matches this year because of injury. The 22-year-old’s results away from the majors – including titles in Cincinnati and Barcelona – have been nearly as eye-catching as his MASSIVE forehand (unlike many French players, he’s all about firepower rather than feel).
 But … and it’s a big but … Zverev’s serve has been imperious on this lightning-fast indoor court at the Inalpi Arena and I’m not sure Fils has the consistency on his return to combat that – especially as he needs to win in straight sets. Two tie-breaks may represent Fils’ best chance – but he’s also got to find a way of taking care of his own serve – and in this breakout season for him, such a result would arguably be the most impressive of the lot.
 Play begins: not before 7.30pm GMT/8.30pm local time. Rimani sintonizzato !
